knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the costs of all paid hours must be recovered from the billable hours, so the rate is built from billable hours. Dividing by all paid hours, or using a website average or competitor's rate, does not do this.
The lesson says travel, set-up and admin time does not shrink with the size of the job, so a minimum charge covers the time to attend the site and start work.

The lesson says to build the base rate from your own costs and billable hours, then compare it with the vendor range and local evidence. A national average from another trade or a bidding listing is not a sound source.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate the paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, admin, marketing, training and leave to find the billable hours.
